milestone_brief:
Fix arXMCP#382 — `_declaration_names` drops `set_option … in theorem` and `open … in theorem` declaration sites, so an unaudited declaration can ride inside a clean `axiom_audit` verdict.

DEFECT (verified against this tree). `_DECL_SITE_RE` in `server/handlers/lean_verify.py` anchors at `^\s*`, then optional `@[...]`, then optional modifiers from `_DECL_MODIFIERS`, then a keyword from `_DECL_KEYWORDS`. `set_option` and `open` appear in neither list, so a line beginning with either matches NO site at all: `sites` is never incremented, and the sites-vs-names fail-safe (`sites == len(names)`) therefore reports complete. When the snippet also contains at least one recognised declaration, `names` is non-empty, the caller proceeds, and the unrecognised declaration is never passed to `#print axioms`.

Observed:
  plain (control)                          -> names=['harmless'] complete=True
  "set_option ... in theorem sneaky" + thm -> names=['harmless'] complete=True   <- sneaky DROPPED
  "open Classical in theorem sneaky" + thm -> names=['harmless'] complete=True   <- sneaky DROPPED
  set_option ... in <thm>   (alone)        -> names=[]           complete=True   <- fine: caller emits _audit_unknown
  multiline `open X in` on its own line    -> names=['fine']     complete=True   <- fine, unaffected

The empty-names path is NOT the bug: the caller hits `if not names:` and emits `_audit_unknown`, which is honest abstention per CLAUDE.md 4.9 rule 2 and must be left alone. The bug is strictly the MIXED case, and it needs the `... in` prefix on the SAME line as the declaration keyword — the common Mathlib idiom `set_option maxHeartbeats 400000 in theorem ...`.

WHY IT MATTERS. `axiom_audit` is the axis that closed the founding `status:"ok"` conflation (issues #205/#281/#332); CLAUDE.md 4.9 rule 1 and the verification-contract track both lean on it. A declaration that declares its own axiom can currently pass through inside a verdict reported as clean.

FIX (conservative, per the issue). Treat an unrecognised prefix before a declaration keyword as a SITE WITHOUT AN EXTRACTABLE NAME, so `sites > len(names)` and the existing fail-safe forces `complete=False` (the caller then emits `_audit_unknown`). Do NOT teach the regex `set_option` / `open` grammar — preserve the design intent that an unrecognised site fails safe rather than being parsed. Fail-safe over feature.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA.
1. Given a snippet with `set_option ... in theorem X` on one line plus a second recognised theorem, when `_declaration_names` runs, then it returns complete=False (not a silent drop), and the caller emits `_audit_unknown` rather than a clean audit.
2. Same for `open ... in theorem X`.
3. The existing honest-abstention path is unchanged: a snippet with ONLY an unrecognised-prefix declaration still yields empty names and `_audit_unknown`.
4. Controls do not regress: a plain declaration, a declaration with a recognised modifier (private, noncomputable, ...), an `@[simp]` attribute line, and a multi-line `open X in` followed by the declaration on the NEXT line all still return their names with complete=True.
5. Regression fixture covers all of the above; `ruff check .` clean and the full pytest suite green.

CONSTRAINTS. `assert` is banned outside `tests/**` (ruff S101, CLAUDE.md 4.7). No behaviour change to `status` / `compilation_success`. If the tool DESCRIPTION or the frozen schema would change, that is a TOOL_SCHEMA_VERSION re-pin per CLAUDE.md 9 — but a pure fail-safe tightening should not touch either; confirm rather than assume.
